function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below you’ll find everything you need to get **nodejs‑welcome** running inside a container, exposed through Kubernetes, and automatically built whenever something lands on `main`.  
I’ve written the artefacts from scratch – feel free to tweak paths, ports, or image tags to match your exact setup.

> ⚠️ **Important:** These snippets are meant to be copied into your local copy of the repo after you have cloned it (`git clone …`). They don’t touch the remote until you run the last few Git commands yourself.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the Repository  

```bash
# SSH key required → make sure ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub is added to GitHub
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

If you prefer HTTPS:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse & Generate Artefacts  

### 2.1 Dockerfile  
Assuming the repo contains a standard Node Express app under `/src` and uses environment variable `PORT` (or defaults to `3000`)…

Create **`docker/Dockerfile`** (you may also put it at the repo root – pick one convention):

```dockerfile
# Stage 1 – build
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Install dependencies first (caching)
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm install --omit dev && \
    rm -rf ./tmp/*

# Copy source
COPY . .

# Expose runtime port
ENV NODE_ENV production
ARG APP_PORT=3000
ENV PORT=${APP_PORT}
EXPOSE ${APP_PORT}

# Run the app
USER node
ENTRYPOINT [ "npm", "start" ]
```

*Why this layout?*

| Layer | Reason |
|-------|--------|
| `builder` | Uses lightweight Alpine, caches deps |
| `NODE_ENV=production` | Avoides installing dev‑deps in prod |
| `--omit dev` | Keeps image lean |
| `USER node` | Runs without root privileges |

Feel free to change `node:20-alpine` to whatever LTS you prefer.

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes Yaml(s)  

#### 2.2.1 Deployment (`k8s/deployment.yaml`)
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 3          # Adjust scaling here
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/<YOUR_GH_USERNAME>/nodejs-welcome:<TAG>
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000     # matches Docker EXPOSE
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: nodejs-config
              key: NODE_ENV
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nodejs-config
data:
  NODE_ENV: "production"
```

#### 2.2.2 Service (`k8s/service.yaml`)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80           # Ingress / LoadBalancer sees this
    targetPort: 3000   # Container’s internal port
  type: ClusterIP       # Change to NodePort/LoadBalancer if needed
```

Place both files under a folder called `k8s/` (create it if missing).

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions Workflow (`/.github/workflows/build.yml`)

This CI pipeline does:

1. Checkout code
2. Set up Node and Docker
3. Cache NPM modules
4. Build Docker image
5. Push image to GHCR (optional – remove if you’re not publishing)
6. Optionally run tests

```yaml
name: Build & Publish

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build-and-publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      packages: write         # Needed for GHCR push
      id-token: write         # Optional – for OIDC auth

    steps:
    - name: Check out repository
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Setup Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version-file: '.nvmrc'
        cache: npm

    - name: Install Dependencies
      run: npm ci

    - name: Test (if applicable)
      run: npm test || true   # Skip if no tests

    - name: Log in to GitHub Packages
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build Docker Image
      run: |
        IMAGE_NAME="ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${GIT_SHA}"
        echo "$IMAGE_NAME"
        docker build -t "$IMAGE_NAME" -f docker/Dockerfile .
      
    - name: Push Docker Image
      run: |
        IMAGE_NAME="ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${GIT_SHA}"
        docker push "$IMAGE_NAME"

    - name: Output Image Tag
      run: echo "::notice::Image pushed: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${GIT_SHA}"

env:
  GIT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}   # Short SHA for tagging
```

> **Tip:** If you don’t want to publish to GHCR, comment out the login, build, and push steps, leaving only the Docker build step for local testing.

--- 

## 3️⃣ Stage All New Files

After creating the above directories/files, run:

```bash
git add docker/Dockerfile k8s/*.yaml .github/workflows/build.yml
```

(Adjust glob patterns if you placed files elsewhere.)

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & Push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

Once the push completes, GitHub Actions will kick off immediately, building the image and (optionally) pushing it to GHCR. Your new Kubernetes resources can now be applied with:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/
```

That’s it! 🎉 Feel free to tailor replica counts, image names, or service types to fit your cluster strategy. Happy coding!
